title: Hines's later show business
summary: They agree Hines's later shows have too much showbiz.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Yeah, Earl later on had -- didn't he have some girls that played fiddle, or something?
Yeah, that was way after me. He had -- in fact, I think he had an all girl band, didn't he? Out here at El Grotto, or something? 64th and Cottage. Yeah, well, that was way after me.
Earl -- I wish Earl would forget show business and just play piano. I love to hear him play piano, but I don't like to go and hear him because I've got to go through all that show business.
He still thinks he's at the Grand Terrace.
Did you catch him at the Ritz?

No, no, I didn't. I was out of town most of that time. But I knew what it would be, you know. All the singers, and -- I saw him one time at the -- what was this hotel out at 47th and South Park? The Sutherland.

Yeah, 47th and Drexell. He came in with a band, and this was in the sixties, and he had an organ player, and he had Vi Redd on alto saxophone, a girl who plays very good alto. And a couple of singers. But it was just too much show business, not enough music. But I
guess that does stem from the early days at the Grand Terrace.
